title: Open Return Authorization Holdback on Final Rebate Checks — Contract Pricing Agreement
content:
**Open return authorization holdback — Contract Pricing Agreement final rebate check**

The open-return holdback follows the customer's most recently authorized return, as the customer's Ship-To Fulfillment Account records show it, while no receipt, decline or no-credit closing has been recorded for that return. Calendar days from one date to another count the later date and not the earlier one. Wherever a latest or most recent record of a kind is taken, it is the one with the latest date, and among records of the same date the one recorded first.

| Most recently authorized return | Open-return holdback |
|---|---|
| Unsettled, reason ordered in error or no longer needed | The authorized quantity multiplied by the invoiced unit price, multiplied by the rebate rate of the agreement's latest accrual and divided by 100 |
| Unsettled, reason defective item or damaged in transit | 0.5 times that figure |
| Unsettled with any other reason, or settled (a receipt, decline or no-credit closing recorded), or no authorized return | None |

The amount is held back from the unpaid rebate balance before the final check's floor at 0.00, its rounding to the cent and its minimum payout test are applied; what is held back stays in the rebate balance.

Hypothetical example: an unsettled authorization for 40 units invoiced at 12.50, reason no longer needed, with a latest accrual rate of 1.5 percent, holds back 40 multiplied by 12.50 (500.00), multiplied by 1.5 and divided by 100: 7.50. Had the reason been damaged in transit, the holdback would be 3.75.
